sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the informant.

2. The petitioner is an accused in C.T. Case No.1893 of 2020 corresponding to C.T. Spl. Case No.9 of 2021, pending on the file of learned Adhoc Additional District & Sessions Judge,(FTSC), Jajpur,
arising out of Jajpur Road P.S. Case No.524 of 2020 for commission of alleged offences under Sections 363/376(3)/376(2)(n) of IPC read with Section 6 of POCSO Act.
3.

Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Adhoc Additional District & Sessions Judge,(FTSC), Jajpur, by order dated 26.11.2022 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the petitioner is in custody since 09.01.2021 and since the victim and her parents have been examined in the meanwhile, further continuance of the petitioner in custody is unwarranted.
5. Learned counsel for the State and informant oppose the prayer for bail inter alia on the ground that releasing the petitioner at this stage will derail the ongoing trial.
6. This Court perused the deposition of the victim, which is taken on record.

8. Additionally, it is directed that the petitioner shall not leave the territorial jurisdiction of the learned Court in seisin without its express permission and shall appear before the jurisdictional police station once every week on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.
Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the learned Court in seisin.
9. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
10. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per the rules.
